candidates.name: Belgrade Cathedral
candidates.content: The Cathedral Church of St Michael the Archangel is Orthodox, built 1837-40 in neoclassical style with a richly-decorated interior. Buried in front of the church are two notable Serbian linguists, Vuk Karadžić and Dositej Obradovi

candidates.name: Historical Museum of Serbia
candidates.content: Huge collection of materials about the Serbian nation from ancient times to the present. In the coming years it's intended to move to new premises on the site of the former railway station.

candidates.name: Nikola Tesla Museum
candidates.price: English guided tour RSD800, cash only
candidates.content: Nikola Tesla (Никола Тесла, 1856-1943) made huge contributions to electric engineering, pioneering alternating current (enabling long-distance high-energy transfer), radio (underpinning today's mobile comms) and AC motors as used

candidates.name: Temple of Saint Sava
candidates.alt: Hram Svetog Save / Храм Светог Саве
candidates.content: The largest church in Serbia and one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world, under construction since 1935 and still not entirely finished. It's described as a temple (Hram) to distinguish it from the smaller St Sava Church

candidates.name: Museum of Yugoslavia and Tito's Mausoleum
candidates.content: This is in 3 buildings. Old Museum is a general display of the history and culture of the former Yugoslavia. 25 May Museum is an oh-so-Sixties building named for the official birthdate of Josip Broz Tito (1892-1980). It displays p

candidates.name: Ethnographic Museum
candidates.content: Extensive display of Serbian costumes, tools, culture and everyday life in past centuries.

candidates.name: National Museum
candidates.hours: Tue Wed Fri Sun 10:00-18:00, Thu Sat 12:00-20:00
candidates.content: Founded in 1844, it has more than 400,000 items on 3 floors. It's organised into Paleolithic, Ancient History, Middle Ages and Modern.

candidates.name: Republic Square
candidates.content: The south side of the National Museum is the city's main plaza. The equestrian statue is of Prince Mihailo Obrenović (1823-1868), who negotiated the withdrawal of Ottoman troops from Belgrade. The city Cultural Centre also fronts

candidates.name: Sukat Shalom Synagogue
candidates.content: Sephardic Jews settled in Belgrade from the 16th century, as the Ottomans welcomed those fleeing Spanish persecution. The Ashkenazis arrived in numbers from the 19th century, escaping Tsarist Russia, and completed this synagogue i

candidates.name: St Mark's Church
candidates.alt: Crkva Sv Marka / Црква Св Марка
candidates.content: Large Serbian Orthodox church built 1931-40 in Serbo-Byzantine style. Within are the tombs of King Stefan Uroš IV Dušan (1308-55), and of King Aleksandar I Obrenović (1876-1903) and his Queen Draga Mašin.

candidates.name: Aeronautical Museum
candidates.content: Closed for rebuilding until 2027. The main collection is in a striking geodesic glass building, with additional aircraft displayed on the surrounding grounds. The museum has over 200 aircraft flown by the Serbian and Yugoslav Air

candidates.name: Bajrakli Mosque
candidates.content: Built around 1575 when Islam was the majority religion, it's now the only mosque in Belgrade. Bajrakli means "with flag" - the muwaqqit calculated the exact time of Islamic observances and hoisted a flag to advise the other city m

candidates.name: Church of St Alexander Nevsky
candidates.content: This Orthodox church was completed in 1929, replacing that of 1877. It has notable relics and frescoes.

candidates.name: Church of the Intercession of the Holy Virgin
candidates.content: Small Orthodox church built in 1933, in simple Serbian-Byzantine style. It's adorned with frescoes and mosaics, and has a rich collection of relics.

candidates.name: Rakovica Monastery
candidates.content: Built on its present site from 1600, the monastery's main structure is the Church of Archangel Michael. The other churches are modern.

candidates.name: Belgrade Zoo
candidates.content: Popular, but with a lot of animals in a small space.

candidates.name: Residence of Princess Ljubica
candidates.content: Built in 1830 as a grand residence for Ljubica Vukomanović (1788-1843), consort of Prince Miloš Obrenović. It remained in royal use to 1842. Since 1979 it's been a branch of the City Museum, exhibiting architecture and furnishings

candidates.name: Royal Palace
candidates.content: Residence of the royal family of Serbia. You can only visit on a guided tour (in English or Serbian), booked through the Tourist Information Offices. The tour takes in the White Palace, with a large art collection.

candidates.name: White Hill
candidates.hours: Apr-Oct Tue Wed Fri 10:00-16:00, Thu 12:00-18:00, Sat Sun 10:00-18:00
candidates.content: A large tell, a 10 m hillock of prehistoric settlements, mostly Neolithic. At weekends there are guided tours through the site.

candidates.name: Chinese Cultural Centre, Belgrade
candidates.content: A cultural centre built on the former site of the Chinese embassy to Yugoslavia, which was bombed by NATO forces in a so-called miscalculated operation in 1999. There is a plaque commemorating the Chinese journalists who died in t

candidates.name: Military Museum
candidates.content: Extensive collection of Serbia's military history. Good signage in English.

candidates.name: Museum of the Serbian Orthodox Church
candidates.content: Museum of church history with frescoes, mosaics, and icons. Good signage in English.

candidates.name: Museum of Applied Art
candidates.content: Displaying art and design from early history.

candidates.name: Zepter Museum
candidates.content: Modern Serbian art.

candidates.name: Chocolate Museum
candidates.content: Chocolate's role in the story of the city, and you get to make your own.

candidates.name: Museum of Science and Technology
candidates.content: Gadgets, transport and machinery down the ages.

candidates.name: Museum of Illusions
candidates.content: Family-friendly place with all the fairground usuals: distorting mirrors, Ames Room, and so on.

candidates.name: Old Palace
candidates.content: This was the residence of the Obrenović and Karađorđević princely dynasties from 1884 until 1922. It now houses Belgrade City Assembly, no visits except on business.

candidates.name: Public Observatory
candidates.content: Four small telescopes enable daytime viewing of the city. On F Sa evenings from 20:30 if the sky is clear you can use the 110/2050 mm refractor and 200/2000 mm reflector for night viewing, with commentary and guidance from staff.

candidates.name: National Theatre
candidates.content: This puts on opera, ballet and theatre. The main hall is worth looking in at, decorated with gilt and artwork.

candidates.name: Blaznavac
candidates.content: Courtyard café-bar with eclectic decoration, serving cocktails, beer and coffee.

candidates.name: Demokratija bar
candidates.content: Cocktail and wine bar serving cocktails and house infusions, with a smoke-free interior and outdoor seating.

candidates.name: Riddle Bar
candidates.content: Speakeasy-style cocktail bar without a fixed menu; bartenders suggest drinks based on the guest's preferences.

candidates.name: Black Turtle
candidates.content: One of several Black Turtle brewery pubs. House beers include fruit-flavoured variants; this branch has outdoor tables with river views.

candidates.name: Dogma Brewery Central
candidates.content: Brewery taproom with eight rotating taps, canned releases, bar food and a small courtyard.

candidates.name: Gecko
candidates.content: Irish-style pub on the central pedestrian café strip.

candidates.name: Publin
candidates.content: Small neighbourhood pub with rock music and Serbian beer.

candidates.name: Three Carrots Irish Pub
candidates.content: Irish pub with draft beer, televised sport and occasional live or acoustic music.

candidates.name: Zuzu's
candidates.content: Café-bar and kitchen with outdoor tables on Obilićev Venac.

candidates.name: Znak Pitanja
candidates.content: Traditional Serbian cuisine. Try ćevapčići sa kajmakom (grilled minced meat with cream), or if you have an adventurous stomach, try young bull's sex glands & bowels.

candidates.name: KMN
candidates.content: Great selection of domestic cuisine, including veggie. Friendly efficient staff.

candidates.name: Roll Bar
candidates.content: Good quality, sizable portions. Try the imperial chicken and feta chicken.

candidates.name: Pizzeria Trg
candidates.content: Delicious pizza and pancakes. Cash only.

candidates.name: Yalla Yalla
candidates.content: Lebanese food.

candidates.name: Skadarlijske kobasice
candidates.content: Excellent sausages.

candidates.name: Giros tim
candidates.content: Good gyros.

candidates.name: Amigo
candidates.content: Very good fried pancakes.

candidates.name: Gastroteka
candidates.content: Serbian fast food.

candidates.name: Jazzayoga
candidates.content: Sandwiches, wraps, juices, and baked goods, relaxing ambience.

candidates.name: Sinđelić
candidates.content: Traditional Serbian cuisine.

candidates.name: Mika Alas
candidates.content: Try their delicious fish soup "riblja čorba" and their house specialty, "smuđ romanov", Pike Perch fillet in white wine cream sauce. Excellent food for an acceptable price.

december.text: National Bank of Serbia has a visitor centre and museum at Kralja Petra 12, a block east of the cathedral. You get to print banknotes with your own face: with the advent of cryptocurrency, the bank probably thought "what the hell". It's open M-F 10:00-16:00.
St Nicholas is an Orthodox church 100 m east of Gardoš Tower at Njegoševa 43. It was completed in 1752.
Ice skating: Winter City Ada is by the east road link, see below for other city sites.
Ice skating is available in winter at Ada Ciganlija as above, in Trg Nikole Pašića, at Pionir Ice Hall and Olimp Sports Centre.
Znak Pitanja: Traditional Serbian cuisine. Try ćevapčići sa kajmakom (grilled minced meat with cream), or if you have an adventurous stomach, try young bull's sex glands & bowels.
